=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

**Overall:** The Seller's cover note calls the package "fair and balanced". It isn't. The Seller Update also contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. The Update says Bluefen is "addressed" and the Riverlark and bonus items are handled, but the Disclosure Letter admits there is no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark repayment or discharge, and no bonuses in the funds flow. The data-room cut-off (22 Sept 2026) is also stale, so we need a bring-down.

Dollar figures below are the Seller's own. The percentage and arithmetic figures are mine.

---

### Warranty and liability framework

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap (opening ask 50%, or 100% of price), with separate and higher caps for fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. Open at 50% and treat 30% as the floor, because 20% is thin against a business with 30% customer concentration and live IP and privacy issues.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis (about AUD 10k) with related claims aggregated, and a tipping (first-dollar) basket of about AUD 120k.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. A deductible basket combined with a high de minimis strips out most realistic claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties (two audit cycles), longer periods for tax and fundamental claims, and no period applying to fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "applies to all Claims" default and counter at 24 months. As drafted, that default would silently shorten every other regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties capped and time-limited like general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price (or uncapped up to proceeds), no de minimis or basket, and a long-stop of at least 6 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A title failure goes to the root of the deal, and the convenience argument doesn't justify cutting protection.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Silent. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature", which arguably captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so no cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause limits claims for fraud, dishonest concealment or wilful misconduct, including by the Seller's officers and agents.
- **Recommendation:** Insert it. Silence plus "all Claims of any nature" is a drafting gap that favours the Seller.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, with fair detail, against identified warranties. No general disclosure against fundamental, tax or indemnity items. A bring-down to signing and Completion. The data room limited to a agreed index and USB copy.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Blanket data-room disclosure would gut the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete it. Add an express pro-sandbagging clause so that Buyer knowledge doesn't reduce its rights. At most, accept actual knowledge of the named deal team about a specifically and fairly disclosed matter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. "Discoverable" imports constructive knowledge and, with SPA-N-006, would defeat nearly every claim. Known issues should be handled through specific indemnities, conditions and price, not warranties.

---

### Specific deal issues

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours", and the consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. The Disclosure Letter admits no consent or evidence of satisfied conditions has been delivered (DD-002, cl 11.2/11.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An unconditional condition precedent. The consent must be written, unconditional (or on terms acceptable to the Buyer), and satisfy the cl 11.3 conditions. Only the Buyer can waive it. Include a long-stop date and a termination right.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30%, of FY26 revenue, so the consent is core value.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion". About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and not repaid (DD-003).
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the price. Payout letter and discharge of security (including PPSR and any ASIC charges) delivered at Completion, in escrow if needed. Riverlark's cl 8.1 change-control addressed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. This is a debt-free deal, so debt must be paid off and security released at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420k is "a matter for the Seller" and is not in the funds flow (DD-005).
- **Buyer wants:** Treat the bonuses as debt-like or transaction costs, deducted from price or paid by the Seller through the funds flow. Include payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, which the Seller hasn't quantified.
- **Recommendation:** Require it in the funds flow. If it's the Seller's problem, it must be settled out of the Seller's proceeds, not left with the Company.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
- **Facts:** AUD 180k is recorded as open (DD-010), unverified by bank evidence. Under cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. No receipt or confirmatory assignment exists.
- **Buyer wants:** Payment evidenced and a confirmatory IP assignment as a condition or Completion deliverable. A broader indemnity covering ownership, title and any third-party claims over the Project Materials, outside the cap, basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The risk is loss of IP ownership, not just AUD 180k.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (SPA cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. The export may hold about 1,240 records (names, emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligations are unresolved.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity for investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory and third-party costs. Seller to complete the investigation and the Privacy Act eligible-data-breach assessment before Completion and share the results. Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. Check the statutory assessment timeline now: the incident predates 22 Sept, so the 30-day assessment window may have already run.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k (3 × AUD 110k) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Facts:** The Disclosure Letter doesn't say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and the Seller Update's label isn't backed by it.
- **Buyer wants:** Terms and status of each renewal. Treat any prepaid, accrued or committed amount as debt-like or a working-capital adjustment. A pre-Completion covenant not to renew or commit without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Hold the point. Don't accept the "ordinary course" label until the Seller documents it.

---

### Structure and verification

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** One undifferentiated regime. Limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate tiers for (1) general warranties, (2) fundamental/title, (3) tax, (4) specific indemnities and price/leakage claims, and (5) fraud. Each tier has its own cap, thresholds and time limit, and the general limits expressly don't apply to tiers 2–5.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. This is the structural fix that resolves N-001 to N-005.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The Disclosure Letter says this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification".
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC current and historical extracts, share certificates, transfer and issue history, constitution and pre-emption rights, PPSR and any Riverlark share security, and no options or encumbrances. Full title guarantee warranty with the fundamental-tier protection from N-004.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register alone. Complete verification and make it a CP or Completion deliverable.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP positions "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity plus tax warranties, running at least 6 years or the ATO amendment period (confirm the applicable period). IP warranties on ownership, contractor and employee assignments, open-source use and non-infringement, at a higher cap or fundamental tier.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Nothing in the documents supports it, and it is not resolved by the general regime.

---

### Other points to confirm
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** Neither disclosure says consent is required on a share sale, but confirm against the underlying clauses and obtain written confirmation or an acknowledgement rather than relying on silence.
- **Disclosure Letter cl 1.4 and 11:** The non-admission language is acceptable, but cl 11 shouldn't be read as the Seller conceding the Buyer's entitlements. Make sure the SPA says disclosure doesn't limit specific indemnities.
- **Price exposure:** The Seller's own figures show up to about AUD 4.13m of items (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 420k, Sandbar 330k, Ironquay 180k) that the Seller Update either defers, pushes to the Buyer, or understates. Not all are price reductions, but all need allocation in the funds flow.

**Next steps:** I can draft the SPA mark-up language for the tiered liability regime, fraud carve-out, and specific indemnities, plus a Completion deliverables list and a CP schedule. Tell me which to start with.
